article.title: “Shameful”: Fossil Fuel Industry Blocks U.N. Climate Action as Global Warming Reaches 1.5°C
article.content: As Democracy Now! continues broadcasting from the U.N. climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, we speak with Rachel Cleetus, climate program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists, about climate finance — the notion that efforts to mitigate the climate crisis must be funded. “Climate finance is not an abstract thing. It’s what countries need to be able to transition away from fossil fuels,” says Cleetus. “And right now we have pennies in these funds.” She notes that at a pledging event for the Adaptation Fund, which supports climate finance for developing countries, a mere $50 million was pledged. “It’s shameful, absolutely unjust, what’s happening here. And richer countries are continuing to block progress.” This comes as scientists say the world is set to overshoot the target, set by the 2015 Paris Agreement, of limiting global heating to 1.5 degrees Celsius. Page 2 Ecuadorians voted overwhelmingly in 2023 to stop oil extraction at Yasuní National Park, one of the most biodiverse places on Earth, yet oil drilling has continued despite that historic referendum. “The government does not want to close the wells,” says Ivonne Yánez, the president of Acción Ecológica, an environmental nonprofit group based in Ecuador. The Ecuadorian government is also “continuing expanding the oil activities in the Amazon,” she points out. Yánez also speaks about how dangerous Latin America is for environmental activists. It is where “the most number of defenders that are just defending their lands, their rivers, their rights,” are killed. “And in Ecuador, this is also happening.”
